Nasdaq recovered 1.09% Friday but declined 3.4% over the week; the daily bounce is not a weekly reversal.
US equities and Brazilian equities rose Friday while Nikkei and Kospi each fell about 6%; global financial stress is differentiated.
Treasury nominal yields rose 5bp 2y and 2bp 10y but the Fed did not change its policy rate on November 6.
Brent fell heavily over the week while tanker threats and freight constraints persisted; no direct measure of global physically delivered barrels provided.
October China manufacturing PMI was below 50 while US labor hiring picked up; the global growth cycle is not homogeneous.
limitations: Market cutoff 7 November 2026 00:55 BRT; latest complete equities, currency and oil sessions are 6 November Friday.
October US BLS survey preliminary and subject to later revision; payroll, unemployment and part-time work are different statistical series.
AP index returns and values may differ slightly from some data vendors with alternate cutoff conventions; the report uses one stated AP print.
Treasury par curve is constant-maturity nominal yield, not executable bond transaction or actual Fed target rate.
Brent/WTI settlement is a futures contract; shipping incidents are attributed reports, not independently verified identities or volume losses.
Euro-area October HICP is a flash estimate and UK mid-2027 inflation an official forecast, not a realized observation.
Asian equities approximated from closing reports; underlying index composition and currency differ.
Market-implied Dec FOMC rate probabilities reflect instrument models, not an official FOMC forecast.
